actual_checks: Full exact prompt, API/meta, report and source/provenance read; no prior listed. The partial scope retains the specified-point quantifier for smooth Hamiltonian inputs on compact symplectic surfaces. It does not replace arbitrary finite-Cr inputs or the flow/high-dimensional problem.

Asaoka–Irie gives a periodic point in any prescribed nonempty open U after arbitrarily small smooth Hamiltonian perturbation. A decreasing neighborhood basis of f and shrinking U_j gives f_j->f and q_j->p simultaneously.

With i_X omega=-dH and H=chi(v_y*x-v_x*y), on the cutoff-one region X=(v_x,v_y); the full segment from 0 to v_j is contained there. The fixed cutoff yields all derivative bounds O(|v_j|), so time-one maps psi_j tend smoothly to identity and send p to q_j.

Conjugation g_j=psi_j^-1*f_j*psi_j remains Hamiltonian, tends smoothly to f, and makes p periodic with the period of q_j. No bound on periods is asserted. Finite total area excludes wandering open sets, so every point of the stated input lies in the required nonwandering set. Smooth convergence only gives finite-Cr neighborhoods of this smooth input.
